item.title: 2,800-year-old Siberian tomb reveals 1,000 cannabis seeds and evidence of ritual intoxication
item.description: A groundbreaking archaeological find at Tunnug 1 in southern Siberia unveiled cannabis seeds within a prince's tomb, dating back 2,800 years. This tomb is tied to intricate funerary rites, including horse sacrifices. Notably, preserved human hair revealed traces of cannabis, hinting at its psychoactive use, which underscores cannabis's significant role in ancient burial customs. Researchers plan to conduct further DNA analysis to deepen the understanding of its historical relevance.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: New Mexico artist gives a 1953 Chevy Bel Air a second life as a jackrabbit
item.description: Robert Wilson crafted an impressive sculpture of a jackrabbit from salvaged components of a 1953 Chevrolet Bel Air. Titled Run, this artwork symbolizes the rich heritage of Route 66 through its creative design. Towering at over 10 feet, it is richly detailed to reflect its automotive origins. Situated in Babe Ruth Park, Gallup, this piece celebrates the 100th anniversary of the legendary highway, inviting visitors to appreciate its artistry.

item.title: Omaha apartment owner's civil rights lawsuit over 2018 closure rejected by appeals court
item.description: A federal appeals court confirmed the dismissal of civil rights claims by AB Realty against Omaha officials. The lawsuit arose after the city shut down a building due to code violations in 2018. Despite the claims alleging Fourth, Fifth, and Fourteenth Amendment violations, the court found insufficient evidence to support them. The ruling highlighted that the city had acted according to legal standards during the inspections.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Azores Glider Emergency Landing: Fuel leak turns A330 into 65-nautical-mile glider; all 306 survive
item.description: In August 2001, an Air Transat flight traveling from Canada to Portugal experienced a dramatic failure, losing both engines mid-flight. The skilled pilots successfully glided for 19 minutes before executing an emergency landing at Lajes Air Base in the Azores. Remarkably, all 306 on board survived despite injuries from the hard landing.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Birds flap their wings while landing even though it costs energy, new model explains why
item.description: Research shows that birds flap their wings while landing to enhance control and deceleration. The energy expended during flapping has tangible benefits for a safe landing. Mathematical modeling indicates that a zero-speed landing without flapping is impractical for most birds. Birds of prey may also swoop to manage touchdown speed and avoid stalling before landing.

item.title: Louisiana court backs homeowner's right to block neighbours from private road beyond 1,000 feet
item.description: Mona Matherne spent over a decade contesting neighbors' use of a private road beside her country home. In November 2026, state appeals judges upheld her property rights and confirmed previous court orders. Matherne successfully argued against her neighbors, who claimed the road was public. The court ruled that only the first 1,000 feet was public, protecting Matherne's privacy.

item.title: Ohio man keeps premarital home as court upholds $20,000 legal-fee award against ex-wife
item.description: The Ohio Court of Appeals has upheld that a husband retains ownership of his pre-marriage house, resisting claims from his ex-wife. The judges clarified that the use of rental income for payments did not affect the house's classification as separate property. Moreover, the court ordered his ex-spouse to cover $20,000 in legal fees, highlighting the tensions caused by her legal maneuvers throughout their prolonged dispute.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Ohio homeowner ordered to pay contractor $45,806 despite cosmetic defects in basement walls
item.description: An Ohio homeowner was ordered to pay a contractor $45,806 for a concrete foundation with cosmetic flaws. The court found that structural integrity was maintained, despite visible surface defects. The homeowner had initially refused payment, claiming that the imperfections reduced property value. The appeals court upheld the lower court decision, emphasizing the importance of structural safety over cosmetic issues.

item.title: North Dakota woman loses $110,000 home improvement claim after breakup with partner
item.description: After her relationship concluded, Mary Roth pursued the return of over $110,000 she invested in home enhancements. However, the North Dakota Supreme Court determined that she could not secure restitution through an unjust enrichment claim. The ruling underscored that Roth needed to demonstrate an actual financial benefit to the property owner, something her receipts failed to do when it came to increasing the property's market value.

item.title: West Virginia court overturns $31,054 home value payout but protects wife's mortgage share
item.description: The West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals has overturned a previous decision regarding a premarital home. The court ruled that the husband is not liable for the home's market value increase during marriage. This ruling clarifies how separate property and marital contributions are treated in divorce cases. However, the former wife is entitled to financial interest from mortgage principal payments made during the marriage.

item.title: Queen Elizabeth II’s final days at Balmoral Castle: Inside her 53,000-acre Scottish sanctuary
item.description: Queen Elizabeth II spent her final days at Balmoral Castle, her beloved Scottish retreat spanning 53,000 acres. The royal estate held decades of cherished family memories, offering her peace and comfort amid nature. From royal summer holidays to her final moments, discover why Balmoral remained one of the Queen’s most treasured places throughout her life.

item.title: Rare Altdorfer landscape hidden for 70 years after 1957 acquisition could fetch £5 million
item.description: An undiscovered masterpiece by Albrecht Altdorfer, the renowned German Renaissance painter, is set to hit the auction block at Sotheby's this December. This exquisite work, featuring a stunning forest scene crowned by a rainbow, has been held privately since 1957. With Altdorfer's oil landscapes being incredibly scarce, this auction represents a rare chance for collectors, the first of its kind since 1980, including viewings in New York and London beforehand.
